evals.name: triggers-on-32x32-icon-request
evals.prompt: draw a 32x32 icon of a health potion, red liquid in a round glass flask
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:sprite. Takes the size and subject from the request, states any defaulted choices (palette, view, target) in one line instead of interrogating, authors a palette-locked spec with `.` as transparent, renders it with the bundled render.py, reads preview.png and critiques it, then delivers sheet.png at 1x, sheet.json, the preview and the gallery index.html.
expectations: Invokes the sprite skill, not animate or scene
Uses a 32x32 grid as requested
States defaulted choices in one line rather than asking a list of questions
Renders with the bundled render.py and reads preview.png before delivering
Delivers sheet.png at 1x as the asset, not preview.png

evals.name: triggers-on-rpg-maker-face
evals.prompt: make an RPG Maker face for my elf mage, silver hair and green eyes
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:sprite for a character portrait. Reads engine-layouts.md so the face size and sheet layout follow the RPG Maker MZ face convention rather than an arbitrary grid, authors the portrait, runs the render-review loop, and names the delivered files.
expectations: Invokes the sprite skill for a still portrait
Takes the frame size and layout from the RPG Maker entry in engine-layouts.md
Runs at least one render, read, fix round before delivering

evals.name: procedural-generator-for-large-variant-family
evals.prompt: pixel art of a set of 64x64 sword item icons: bronze, iron, gold and crystal variants
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:sprite and chooses the procedural-generator mode because the sprites are large and form a family of variants: a short Python script draws with primitives onto a material grid, maps materials to color ramps, and emits the spec, so each variant is a ramp swap rather than a redrawn grid. The generator is kept beside the output.
expectations: Uses a procedural generator rather than hand-writing 64x64 rows
Makes the variants recolors of one design through material color ramps
Keeps the spec and generator beside the output

evals.name: near-miss-walk-cycle-routes-to-animate
evals.prompt: give my knight sprite a 4-direction walk cycle for Godot
evals.expected_output: Does not fire /pixel-art:sprite: a movement cycle is /pixel-art:animate's job, as the sprite description states. Routes to /pixel-art:animate instead of drawing a single still frame.
expectations: Does not invoke the sprite skill for a walk cycle
Routes to /pixel-art:animate

evals.name: near-miss-title-screen-routes-to-scene
evals.prompt: build an animated title screen for my game with the logo over a pixel-art castle at sunset
evals.expected_output: Does not fire /pixel-art:sprite: an animated title screen is a composed scene, which belongs to /pixel-art:scene. Routes there; a sprite may be authored first only if the scene needs a character that does not exist yet.
expectations: Does not invoke the sprite skill as the handler for a title screen
Routes to /pixel-art:scene

evals.name: near-miss-ink-illustration-not-pixel-art
evals.prompt: draw a hand-inked illustration of a fox in a loose brush-pen style
evals.expected_output: Does not fire /pixel-art:sprite: the request is hand-drawn ink illustration, not a palette-locked pixel grid. Does not force the subject into a pixel sprite; handles the request outside the pixel-art plugin.
expectations: Does not invoke the sprite skill for an ink or brush illustration
Does not convert the request into a pixel-art sprite

evals.name: records-brief-and-grades-done-criteria
evals.prompt: pixel art of a tall lantern-bearing watchman, 32x32, side view. Done when the lantern is the brightest cluster and the silhouette reads at 1x.
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:sprite. Writes brief.md beside the spec before the first render, with proportions, style references, and the two done criteria. Unspecified fields (style references, palette, mood, target) are one defaults line, not questions. Each review round marks every done criterion pass or fail with a one-line reason, and stops when both pass or the round budget is spent with the failures named. A later run that finds that brief.md reads it instead of asking again. Does not call /planning:interview: the subject and done criteria are already stated, and the interview offer is only for a vague or high-stakes request when the planning plugin is installed.
expectations: Writes brief.md beside the spec before the first render
Records proportions and style references, defaulting the ones the request omits in one line
Every review round marks each done criterion pass or fail with a one-line reason
Stops when all criteria pass or the round budget is spent with failures named
Reads an existing brief.md on a re-run instead of re-asking
Does not require /planning:interview; that offer is presence-gated and optional

evals.name: vague-brief-states-defaults
evals.expected_output: Fires /pixel-art:sprite. The request names a subject but no size, palette, view, or done criterion, so it is vague. Offer /planning:interview only if the planning plugin is installed, and do not start it unless the user accepts. Otherwise continue with the in-skill brief: ask only for the subject details that change the pixels, state every other omitted field as a default in one line, and write brief.md with at least the two default done criteria before the first render.
expectations: Invokes the sprite skill
Treats the request as vague because it has no checkable done criterion
Offers /planning:interview only when the planning plugin is installed, and does not start it without acceptance
States omitted fields as defaults in one line
Writes brief.md before the first render
